summary: Worker runtime today = one Go DaemonWorkerRunner (mutex) -> one Python daemon -> one sync-Playwright thread, strictly one job at a time. Python live path already writes events line-by-line, but (a) the engine buffers all pre-submit/token events until after read-back (engine.py:473,614-622,366-367) and (b) Go collects everything until the JOB_END marker (daemonrunner.go:104-128), so nothing is incremental. Recommended lazy design: do NOT thread/async the daemon (sync Playwright is thread-bound, one manager per thread, daemon.py:128-136). Pool = N independent copies of the existing daemon process (Go supervisor, existing stdio protocol unchanged per slot), each pinned to <=1 warm key, plus a physical-session identity gate (Go in-process + Python flock defence-in-depth). Streaming: split engine into pre-submit (buffered, retry-safe) and post-submit (live, never re-submitted). prompt_submitted (already in job-event schema and Go vocab, vocabulary.go:45, no status effect) marks the point of no resubmit. Token events carry attempt_id and are provisional; result comes only from terminal event; JOB_END(status=completed) + exactly one terminal commits, otherwise the attempt is abandoned and gateway appends a failure. Event ids MUST become attempt-scoped: today evt_<sha(job_id:sequence)> (events.py:67) plus ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (jobs/postgres.go:442-452) would silently drop a retry attempt's events (incl. its terminal) once an earlier attempt streamed. Two contradicted plan assumptions found in worker code: false successful truncation (stream_response exits silently at deadline, page_driver.py:1652-1685, engine then emits completed) and blind resubmit (engine retries the whole interaction incl. submit_prompt on any non-drift exception, engine.py:343-352). Biggest hidden isolation hazard: the leaked-tab registry is one file per process ROLE (page_driver.py:1816-1820) and _close_stale_pages (1862-1882, called on every CDP open, 812) closes every registered tab not owned by this process - N same-role processes (pool slots, or UBAG_WORKER_CONCURRENCY>1 per-job live workers today) will kill each other's live tabs. Achievable parallelism is bounded by distinct (provider, physical session) pairs, not CPU: CDP mode reuses browser.contexts[0] and ignores user_data_dir (page_driver.py:805-816). No Rust candidate in this area; Python time is CDP round-trip waits and 0.1-0.4s polls. Plan phase numbers other than 4 are inferred (0 = measure/guard, 1 = contracts, 5 = helper integration).

summary: The 50ms SQL poll is real, and no push mechanism exists anywhere. WaitEvents loops over a two-query listEvents on SQLite and Postgres. The memory store already wakes waiters with one global sync.Cond. Every event write funnels through insertEvent / insertSQLiteEvent, and Postgres assigns per-job sequences under SELECT ... FOR UPDATE. That gives a gap-free, commit-ordered per-job cursor, so a wake-up-then-reread design is safe. Recommended design: a per-job in-process wake hub (the existing WS-5 cap-1 lossy-hint pattern) in all three stores, a Postgres pg_notify on commit plus one dedicated pgx LISTEN connection for multi-replica deployments, and the poll kept as a jittered fallback of about 2s. All of it is gated by env flags that default off. Prod is single-replica (docker-compose.vps.yml) and Helm defaults to 2 replicas (values.yaml:8), so the `local` mode alone covers prod and `postgres` mode is only needed for Helm. Three findings cut the benefit and widen the scope. (a) Worker events reach the store only after the worker exits, and the Python engine itself buffers every token until the interaction ends, so item 3 (incremental streaming) must change the Python engine too, or notify buys nothing for live providers. (b) The SSE handler ignores Last-Event-ID and never closes after a terminal event. (c) There are no tests of WaitEvents, StreamJobEvents or the consumer's exactly-one-terminal validation, so characterization tests must come first.

summary:
RECOMMENDATION: do NOT start a Rust relay experiment yet. Order: (1) reconcile/merge the voice branch and finish live voice acceptance, (2) instrument the relay, (3) apply cheap Python/Go fixes and re-baseline, (4) profile with a pre-registered stop rule, (5) only then consider Rust. A Rust relay is technically plausible (thin glue, std threads, FFI to the same libopus0) but statically the likely gain is small.

REF: all voice code lives only on branch feat/multimodal-voice-hardening (HEAD e0667b5), cited below as VB:path:line. Main has zero voice files and no UBAG_VOICE refs (git grep on main is empty). VB PROGRESS.md:3905-3923 marks the release INCOMPLETE and says do not merge. No relay CPU, memory or latency number exists anywhere; the canary ran 3 frames at 0.5 CPU / 1.5 GiB (VB PROGRESS.md:3765-3794).

PER 20 ms FRAME (50 fps per direction, one session per relay process, VB audio-relay.py:392,655-661):
- Mic (gateway to Chrome):
  - read_frame does 2 recv calls, list+join, then a body[1:] copy (audio-relay.py:146-173).
  - decode allocates a zeroed 11,520 B ctypes array for 1,920 B of output, plus a per-call lock (opus_bridge.py:115-124).
  - native opus_decode runs next, then os.write to the FIFO (audio-relay.py:521).
  - Muted frames are still decoded and discarded (audio-relay.py:512,518).
- Speaker (Chrome to gateway):
  - Reads 1920 B from the parec pipe (audio-relay.py:543).
  - encode allocates an 11,520 B zeroed buffer, then out.raw[:n] copies the whole buffer and slices again (opus_bridge.py:146,155).
  - native opus_encode runs with default ctls and APPLICATION_AUDIO (opus_bridge.py:29,134), 50 times a second even when the provider is silent.
  - write_frame does 2 concatenations plus sendall (audio-relay.py:176-179,554).
- Already native: libopus encode/decode (opus_bridge.py:43-62), PulseAudio, parec. HMAC runs once per session.
- No resampling or channel conversion in the relay: everything is 48 kHz mono s16 (audio-relay.py:106-109,334,411-413).
  - Hypothesis, unverifiable statically: the null sink is created without rate/channels (audio-relay.py:314-316), so PulseAudio may run it at its 44.1 kHz stereo default and resample/downmix in-daemon, possibly a 48k to 44.1k to 48k round trip with Chrome. Check `pactl list short sinks` in the canary. Fixing that is a config change, not Rust.
- GIL contention is likely low and must be confirmed with py-spy --gil. ctypes CDLL calls and syscalls release the GIL, there are 2 pump threads, and the Python sections are tens of microseconds.
- Idle cost: the health thread spawns 2 pactl processes every 5 s forever, and run() wakes every 0.5 s (audio-relay.py:279-293,385-387,464).
- Hypothesis to verify: Python-owned glue is 10-30% of relay CPU and libopus encode dominates. Rust cannot shrink libopus because no mature pure-Rust Opus codec exists, so it would FFI the same library. Relay RSS is tens of MB against a 4096 MiB container capped at 2 CPU (VB docker-compose.vps.yml:279-280) dominated by Chrome. A 25% win on the relay process is therefore very unlikely to be material in a mixed workload.
- p95 latency is queue-bound, not language-bound:
  - Go mic channel is 64 x 20 ms with drop-oldest (VB media.go:64,421-436).
  - TCP socket buffers have no age bound.
  - The mic FIFO is about 64 KiB, roughly 680 ms, and on full it drops the NEWEST frame (audio-relay.py:522-525).
  - The parec pipe holds about 680 ms.
  - Cheap Python lever: fcntl.F_SETPIPE_SZ to shrink both pipes (Python 3.10+, bookworm ships 3.11; verify).

BYTE-IDENTICAL CONTRACT (relay protocol v2, currently only in the docstring, audio-relay.py:15-81, and mirrored in Go media.go:47-73):
- Framing: u32-LE length that includes the type byte, 1 <= len <= 65536, type 0x01 audio or 0x02 control, anything else closes the connection.
- hello JSON fields and validation: session_id str of 1..128 chars, exp int and not bool, exp within [now, now+300], token str.
- Token: hex(HMAC-SHA256(utf8 secret, "voice-relay|{sid}|{exp}")), compared in constant time. Vector: secret "relay-test-secret", sid "s1", exp 1700000000 gives 43e2f2445ad07779cdf6135f4756cbe2ea5802718f6b6b9c930bb67d53a10591. It is asserted ONLY in Go (VB media_relay_test.go:204-209), not in the Python tests.
- Reply JSON must keep compact separators and key order: {"op":"ready"} and {"op":"error","reason":..}.
- 11 handshake reason codes plus devices_lost, monitor_exited and mic_closed: busy, unconfigured, bad_hello, hello_timeout, expired, unauthorized, devices_unavailable, codec_unavailable, mic_unavailable, monitor_unavailable, internal.
- Timing and limits: hello deadline 5 s over the whole frame, at most 4 pending handshakes, 30 s idle (UBAG_VOICE_RELAY_IDLE_S), 8 s device wait (below the gateway's 10 s ready timeout, media.go:58), busy refused before the hello is read, slot freed only after full cleanup.
- Mute: decode-and-discard, applied in frame order. Empty or corrupt packets are dropped without ending the session. Fail closed on an empty secret.
- Known mismatch to pin in fixtures: Go rejects length < 2 (media.go:221) while Python accepts length 1 (audio-relay.py:167).
- Open DTX risk: the 30 s idle timeout against client DTX silence (VB PROGRESS.md:3929). Changing it is a protocol change, not byte-identical.

PROFILING PLAN:
- Prerequisites: real-libopus golden tests (existing tests use FakeLib, VB conftest.py:42-87,198) and env seams for the mic pipe path and the parec/pactl commands.
- Inputs: deterministic seeded corpus of framed v2 streams: 2.5-120 ms packets, silence, corrupt, empty, max-size, mute interleavings; plus a monitor PCM file with a partial final chunk (the zero-pad path, audio-relay.py:548).
- Rig: black-box driver over TCP, parec shim replaying the PCM at 20 ms cadence, FIFO sink writing timestamps to file. It runs unchanged against Python and any Rust binary. Both link the same libopus0 .so (pin the version; vendored builds can change encoder bytes).
- Byte compare: control/handshake replies, FIFO bytes, and speaker packets must be identical. Fall back to a decoded-PCM tolerance only if the libopus build differs.
- Measure:
  - /proc utime+stime per call-minute.
  - RSS/PSS, tracemalloc or heaptrack.
  - ctx switches and syscalls per frame.
  - Frame transit p50/p95/p99/max per direction, plus drops.
  - py-spy --native --gil and perf, to split libopus self-time from glue.
  - fd/thread/child leaks over 100 reconnects plus a 1 h soak.
  - Chaos: kill pulse, kill parec, SIGTERM.
- Run on a dedicated lab helper (2c/4G cgroup 1.5 CPU / 2.5 GiB). Do not use the shared prod VPS (VB PROGRESS.md:3921-3923).
- Mixed run: N mock-provider browser workloads plus one voice call, A/B interleaved at least 5 pairs, reporting the CI lower bound. Use a local WebRTC echo page, with no provider login, to respect safe-mode.

GATE (precise):
- U = relay CPU-ms per call-minute minus libopus self-time. Rust needs U <= 0.8 x Python (>= 20% overhead gain), OR relay CPU/RSS <= 0.75 x Python.
- AND materiality: container or host headroom or job p95 improves in the mixed run.
- AND no regression in p95/p99 transit, drops, or leak checks.
- AND the rollback drill passes.

summary:
Verdict: the helper trust plane is greenfield. The main-branch gateway has no in-process TLS, no node identity, no attempt or lease-generation concept and no scoped capability tokens. Several local isolation leaks must be fixed before remote nodes exist.

NEVER-RECEIVE LIST. A helper must never get:
- UBAG_APP_SECRET (serve.go:178,304).
- The Postgres DSN (serve.go:545), MinIO keys (serve.go:602-603), and NATS URL or creds (serve.go:524). nats-mtls.conf has no per-subject authz, so any cert holder can pub/sub every subject.
- UBAG_WEBHOOK_SECRET* (serve.go:1430), UBAG_MASTER_KEK_HEX, the app-JWT private key, SSO/SIEM/MFA secrets, PATs or sessions, and the voice TURN shared secret.
- Other tenants' jobs, the envelope's Callbacks and Client maps, primary-local attachment_local_paths, Antigravity OAuth sockets, and the fleet manager's SSH/WireGuard/Ansible credentials.
- Instead it receives a new per-attempt HelperAttemptSpec type, not DispatchEnvelope. validateLeaseEnvelope (workerconsumer.go:1502-1553) compares callbacks, context and client, so those fields must be dropped by a separate projection.
- The helper env should reuse the minimalWorkerEnv allowlist (workerconsumer.go:1617-1672) minus UBAG_REMOTE_BROWSER_ENDPOINT and UBAG_NOVNC_BASE_URL.

SCOPED CAPABILITIES.
- Reuse the appjwt RS256 sign/verify code (appjwt.go:54-116) with a separate keypair, header typ "ubag-attempt", aud "ubag-helper", and claims {nid, att, gen, jid, tid, keys[], ops, exp<=lease expiry}.
- Do NOT extend AppClaims. resolveAppJWT (server.go:4201-4218) accepts any validly signed token with tid/sub/role/exp, so a shared key would turn attempt tokens into app principals. Make resolveAppJWT reject tokens carrying aud, and add a regression test.
- The token is only a bearer reduction. Every asset RPC also checks the live attempt row (state, generation, node equal to the cert node).
- Hash-at-rest, show-once enrollment and viewer tickets follow the session/pat pattern (session.go:1-12, pat/postgres.go:46). PATs have no job scope (pat.go:19-26), so they are not reusable here.

mTLS identity to node ID.
- Terminate mTLS in-process on a NEW grpc.Server and listener (UBAG_HELPER_GRPC_ADDR) with TLS1.3 and RequireAndVerifyClientCert.
- Never register on the existing grpcServer (serve.go:301). It has no creds, serves reflection (:314), and is exposed through grpcweb on the public mux (:319).
- Never trust the Caddy X-Client-Cert-Subject header (Caddyfile.mtls.example:49). The gateway never reads it.
- The node_id comes from the leaf URI SAN spiffe://ubag/node/<id>, ignoring CN. It is resolved against a primary-owned gateway_helper_nodes table: node_id, spki_sha256 current and next, state, allowed_targets and workloads, registry_digest.
- An interceptor re-checks state on every RPC and stream message, so revocation kills long streams. Any node_id carried in a message must equal the cert-derived id.

ROTATION.
- Certs live <=72h, issued by the shared fleet manager's CA. UBAG runs no CA. The dev gen-certs.sh issues 365d certs and is dev-only.
- The gateway reloads the CA bundle and node table every 30s or on SIGHUP.
- Two pinned fingerprints per node give an overlap window. A reconnecting node resumes by attempt_id plus generation.
- Revocation means deleting the fingerprint, effective within one RPC.

AUDIT.
- The TS vocabulary (audit.ts:4-33) and the authz action list are closed and cross-checked (check-contracts.mjs:275-375), so new names land there first. The Go chain is per tenant (audit.go:23-31). Tenant-bearing events go in the job's chain; node-lifecycle events go in a reserved system tenant "_fleet".
- Events to add: node.enrolled, node.cert_rotated, node.revoked, node.auth_rejected, attempt.granted, attempt.fenced_rejected, attempt.committed, asset.token_issued, asset.read, asset.write, viewer.session_opened, viewer.session_closed, helper.policy_violation.
- The existing authz audit is best-effort (`_, _ =`, server.go:3421). Grants, enrollment and viewer open must use a fail-closed append.

AFFINITY.
- Every identity field comes from the trusted job or attempt record, never helper payload (the pattern at workerconsumer.go:84-92, 711-716, 761-766). Extend it to topology tabs, whose context_id currently comes from the payload.
- The primary computes an opaque profile_ref from a (tenant, provider, identity) binding. It strips options.user_data_dir, profile_dir and profile_path and context.account_binding_id from the helper spec. The helper maps profile_ref to <root>/<tenant_hash>/<provider>/<identity>.
- Conversations gain node_id and profile_ref. A lost node marks the conversation broken; there is no migration.

SAFE MODE ON HELPERS.
- The helper runs the same adapter_registry loader (adapter_registry.py:165-182) and reports registry_digest; the primary compares it.
- payloadpolicy runs on the primary before the spec is built. Every helper event passes the existing sanitizeWorkerData on append (memory.go:415, postgres.go:467, sqlite.go:478).
- No RPC returns profile-dir files. Uploads are limited to artifact kinds the manifest's artifact_policy declares.
- allowed_targets is default-deny. antigravity_cli is ineligible (credentialed OAuth sockets, workerconsumer.go:1279-1297). Only browser adapters with login_posture manual_required, plus mock, are eligible.

MANUAL LOGIN VIEWER.
- Loopback-only today at three layers (engine.py:693-717, jobs/memory.go:703-721, +page.svelte:49-55).
- Production uses a shared nginx Basic Auth credential (default.conf.template:62-117) and VNC -nopw (vps entrypoint.sh:72).
- The helper opens an OUTBOUND OpenViewer stream over its mTLS channel.
- The primary serves a WS proxy behind a single-use ticket bound to operator subject, tenant, node, profile_ref and provider, with exp<=10min and idle 5min. It requires a new browser:interact action (operator and admin only) plus the MFA gate (server.go:3368-3378).
- CDP, VNC and noVNC stay in-container or loopback. Current binds to 0.0.0.0 at small browser-viewer entrypoint.sh:124 and vps entrypoint.sh:176 must not be carried to helpers.
- No programmatic keystroke RPC. Automation is locked out of the profile while a viewer is open, and afterwards only login_state is reported.

FAIL-CLOSED RULES.
- F1: unknown, revoked or mismatched cert, or node state other than active, means no RPC.
- F2: stale generation, expired lease or node mismatch is rejected and audited, never applied.
- F3: any event with a job, tenant or attempt mismatch fails the attempt.
- F4: output over 1MiB or 512 events (workerconsumer.go:97-99) fails the attempt, never success-with-truncation.
- F5: a secret-scan hit means redact, flag and quarantine the node.
- F6: an audit append failure on grant, enroll or viewer open refuses the action.
- F7: when the fleet manager or node cache is unreachable or stale, no new grants; running attempts continue.
- F8: a registry_digest mismatch makes the node ineligible.
- F9: no tenant-matching profile_ref means queue, not assign.
- F10: an expired, replayed or non-MFA viewer ticket is denied.
- F11: an asset key outside the declared manifest or the wrong op returns the same 404 as cross-tenant.
- F12: with UBAG_HELPER_PLANE unset, no listener starts.
- ABAC with a nil or empty bundle is permissive (abac.go:91-95), so fleet actions need an explicit deny-default.
